author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260511T170438Z-856615
text:
Escalating to human after reconnaissance: this bead's premise depends on workspace-wide architectural infrastructure that does not exist and conflicts with the settled foundation design.

# What the bead asks for

A helper `resolve_caller_permissions(backend, caller, account_id, space_id) -> HashSet<String>` that "reads the Space, finds the caller's memberships, unions their roles' permissions plus @everyone defaults" — to gate Space/set patch ops inside `handle_space_set` before calling `backend.apply_space_patch`.

# Why I cannot complete this autonomously

## Finding 1: CallerCtx is opaque and identity-free workspace-wide

Audit of all 8 server crates (jmap-server foundation + 7 extension-server siblings: mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, sharing, filenode):

- `CallerCtx` is declared **once**, on `JmapBackend` in `crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:572`, with bound `Clone + Send + Sync + 'static`. No identity bound. No `caller_id`/`caller_principal`/`whoami` method anywhere on the trait.
- Every extension trait inherits `CallerCtx` via `: JmapBackend` supertrait — none re-declare it or add bounds.
- Every MemoryBackend in all 8 crates binds `type CallerCtx = ()`.
- No handler anywhere extracts identity from `caller` — every use is forwarding. `let _ = caller;` at mail-server/src/sieve.rs:89,109 is the only inspection, and it's a unused-param drop.
- Zero TODO/FIXME comments about this in any .rs file.

The helper the bead asks for **cannot be written** because there is no way to map `&B::CallerCtx` → caller's `Id`.

## Finding 2: The workspace explicitly punts auth to the caller of `dispatch()`

`crate-jmap-server/AGENTS.md` "Design Constraints — Settled — Do Not Revisit" table:

> **Auth: Not in dispatcher — Caller's responsibility — do it before `dispatch()`.**

`backend.rs:529-554` doc-comment reinforces:

> "This is the per-request authentication / authorisation context produced by the caller's auth layer and forwarded unchanged through `Dispatcher::dispatch` → `JmapHandler` → the registered closure → the backend."

This bead is asking to add gates *inside* the dispatch pipeline (handler-side, after parsing patch ops). That contradicts the settled architecture. The workspace's design is: HTTP/auth middleware fully authenticates and authorizes BEFORE the JMAP method even runs, then forwards an opaque `CallerCtx` for the backend to read if it needs per-request context.

## Finding 3: The bead's own parent memory note already flags this

Memory `space-set-structural-mutation-pipeline-bd-jmap-g7wu`:

> ".4.7 and .4.8 (newly filed) because they need **new helper infrastructure** (effective-permission resolver, max-* config source) that .4.2 should not speculatively add."

The memory acknowledges this bead is blocked on "effective-permission resolver" infrastructure. That infrastructure has not been designed.

## Finding 4: The reference impl outside the workspace explicitly disclaims this

`crate-jmapchat-server/jmapchat-server/src/dispatcher.rs:35-42`:

> "# Account access and authorization … **This library does not enforce cross-account authorization.** The application's authentication middleware is responsible for ensuring that the user identified by `account_id` is permitted to access any account they name in requests."

Same model: punt to middleware. No precedent for handler-side gates anywhere in the JMAP ecosystem this workspace is mirroring.

# Three resolution paths (recommendation marked)

## Option A (RECOMMENDED): Close this bead as superseded; move gates into the backend's `apply_space_patch`

The cleanest fix. Permission gating for Space/set patch ops belongs in `MemoryBackend::apply_space_patch` (currently the .4.3/.4.4 backlog), not the handler. That keeps:
- The workspace's settled auth-before-dispatch invariant
- All Space-state reads (members, roles, owner) co-located with the mutations they gate (atomicity)
- Hierarchy enforcement (already a backend responsibility per `backend.rs:176-181`) and permission enforcement together — they share the same Space lookup

What lands now: a pure helper function `required_permissions_for_op(&SpacePatchOp) -> &'static [&'static str]` (the trivial part of this bead, ~30 lines), placed in `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs` or `crate-jmap-chat-types/src/space_set.rs`, with unit tests. Then `.4.3`/`.4.4` consume it inside their `apply_space_patch` implementations.

Trade-off: backends must each re-implement permission lookup, but they already need Space state for hierarchy/owner checks anyway, so it's not duplicate work.

## Option B: Add a default-method `caller_identity` on `JmapBackend`

A surgical workspace-wide extension: add `fn caller_identity(caller: &Self::CallerCtx) -> Option<&jmap_types::Id> { None }` as a default method on `JmapBackend`. Real backends override to return the authenticated user's id; MemoryBackend keeps `None` (meaning "no handler-side identity-based gating possible — backend enforces").

Then this bead can be implemented in the handler as: if `caller_identity` returns `Some`, gate; if `None`, dispatch unconditionally (let backend enforce as before).

Trade-offs:
- Workspace-wide canonical-template change — must propagate to all 7 extension-server siblings (mail-server is canonical per workspace AGENTS.md)
- Mixes auth concerns into the JMAP layer that the foundation explicitly excluded
- Doesn't actually solve the bigger problem (real backends still need Space lookup for hierarchy/owner checks, so they end up doing the work twice — once handler-side for permission gate, once backend-side for hierarchy)

## Option C: Reject this bead's framing, redesign as a workspace-wide auth model

The biggest change: declare that `CallerCtx` carries identity, add bounds (e.g., `CallerCtx: AsRef<Principal>` for some new `Principal` type), and require all backends to implement it. This is the "JMAP server with real auth" design.

Trade-offs:
- Huge breaking change across all 8 server crates
- Probably needs an IETF-level design pass on how JMAP servers represent principals
- Far out of scope for any one bead

# What I am NOT doing

I am NOT implementing Option A unilaterally because:
- It would close this bead as "redirected" without human approval
- The redirect changes .4.3/.4.4 scope (they'd absorb permission gates), which is a parent-epic-level decision
- "Whole-patch reject vs partial reject" is also unresolved (bead recommends whole-patch; needs concurrence)

I am NOT implementing the pure mapping helper alone because:
- It would be dead code without a call site
- Where to put it (chat-server vs chat-types) is itself a design call (the helper takes `&SpacePatchOp` which is in chat-types, suggesting chat-types; but it returns workspace-foreign permission strings, suggesting chat-server)

# Question for human

Pick one of A/B/C (or propose D). My recommendation is **A**: close this bead, redirect the work into `.4.3` and `.4.4` (which are already the backend-side variant implementations), and add a small pure mapping helper as a separate quick bead that .4.3/.4.4 consume.

Releasing the claim and moving to the next ready bead per /do-beads spec.
